1.definition: Greek for "father" (Παππάς) — the affectionate term for a senior churchman that, applied to the bishop of Rome, gives us the English word "pope."

2.definition: Relating to the Huns, the nomadic confederation whose westward push helped shatter the late-antique order; here, the steppe pressure that helped topple the Gupta Empire in India around 550.

3.definition: The duty to welcome and care for travelers and strangers. In early monastic life this was a sacred obligation — the Rule of Benedict commanded that every guest be received as if he were Christ himself.

Literally "pilgrimage for Christ." The Irish monastic practice of permanent self-exile — leaving Ireland forever to preach in foreign lands as a supreme act of ascetic devotion. It is why Irish monks kept turning up founding monasteries everywhere from Burgundy to Iceland.

4.definition: The Latin form of the name Charles. The Frankish ruling house took its dynastic name, Carolingian, from this Latin root — first from Charles Martel's grandfather Charles, and later cemented by Charles Martel himself and his grandson Charlemagne.

6.definition: The Ordinatio Imperii was Louis the Pious's 817 decree spelling out how the Frankish empire would pass to his sons — meant to keep the realm whole under one senior emperor, it instead lit the fuse for decades of civil war among his heirs.

The Normans were the descendants of Vikings who settled in northern France in the early tenth century, took on French language and Frankish customs, and went on to conquer England in 1066 and carve out kingdoms in southern Italy and Sicily — the "Norman south" the chapter points to.

Latin for "rustic Roman language" — the everyday spoken descendant of Latin in the western Frankish lands by the ninth century. Charles the Bald's Strasbourg oath, recorded in it, is the earliest substantial text that reads as French rather than Latin.

7.definition: The coastline of Provence in southeastern France, between the Rhône delta and the Italian border. In the ninth and tenth centuries it was lightly defended and exposed to Saracen raiders operating from the Muslim base at Fraxinetum.
